title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'algèbre des figures'. A 'figure' F on a set S is encoded by a surjection f (also written φ) : S → I onto an ordered index set I. The fibres are the open cells/strata, and the 'étoiles ouvertes' A° (open stars) of the previous page are among the associated subsets. A subfigure G ⊂ F corresponds to a closed part J ⊂ I (closed for the order topology, i.e. an order ideal), with T = |G| = f^{-1}(J) and restricted map f_J = f|T : T → J.

A refinement F' ≤ F, with index set I', is the same as a factorisation S --g--> I' --h--> I of f. Here g is a surjection and h is a monotone 'coinitial' surjection of ordered sets; the precise meaning of 'coinitial' is not defined on this page. Likewise a refinement G' ≤ G is a factorisation T --g_J--> J' --h_J--> J of f_J.

The page translates 'F' induces G'' into these data. There must be an embedding i' : J' ↪ I' such that the two squares commute: S ↩ T over I' ↩ J' (g ∘ incl = i' ∘ g_J), and I' ↩ J' over I ↩ J (h ∘ i' = i ∘ h_J). In addition J' = h^{-1}(J), so the upper square is cartesian: T = g^{-1}(J'). In modern terms, a refinement of a poset-stratified set restricts to the closed substratified set over J by base change along J ↪ I.

Purpose: this sets up the equivalence a) ⇔ b) ⇔ c) ⇔ d) begun on p. 33, characterising when a refinement over a closed part is the restriction of a global one. Page 35 then builds such a global extension explicitly. It forms the poset K = J' ⊔ (I∖J), keeping the given orders on each piece and setting α ≤ β iff h_J(α) ≤ β for α ∈ J', β ∈ I∖J. The map h_K = h_J ⊔ id makes the square with J ↪ I commute, so a refinement of G extends to a refinement of F that changes nothing off G.
errors: Inconsistency in the roles of the two maps. For G', the text attaches 'coinit. surjection d'ens. ordonnés' to g' and plain 'surjection' to h'. For F, it says 'g surj., h coinit. surj.'. By analogy the G' case should presumably read h' coinitial; this looks like a slip of the pen.
Notation drifts on the page: f vs φ, f*_J vs f_J, g*_J vs g_J, h*_J vs h_J. The starred and primed versions denote the same maps.

Commutativity of the squares alone does not force J' = h^{-1}(J); this has to be imposed, and Grothendieck adds it explicitly ('avec J' = h^{-1}(J)'). With it, T = g^{-1}(J') follows. No mathematical error otherwise.

ideas.what: Encoding a cell decomposition / stratification of a set S by a surjection S → I onto a poset; subfigures correspond to closed (down-closed) parts J ⊂ I.
ideas.modern_name: poset-stratified set/space (map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard folklore; formalised e.g. in Lurie, Higher Algebra Appendix A (2010s), and in exodromy work (Barwick–Glasman–Haine)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame stratifications, but not this poset formalism explicitly

ideas.what: Refinements F' ≤ F as factorisations S → I' → I of the stratifying map, with h a coinitial surjection of posets.
ideas.modern_name: refinement of stratifications / stratified map over a poset

ideas.what: Restriction of a refinement to a closed substratum by base change: J' = h^{-1}(J), T = g^{-1}(J'), with commuting squares.
ideas.modern_name: pullback of a stratification along the inclusion of a closed sub-poset

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck works systematically with stratifications as maps to posets, and with refinements as factorisations through poset surjections. This is close to the formalism now standard in higher-categorical stratified homotopy theory (poset-stratified spaces, exodromy). A historian might note it as an unpublished precursor, though the ideas themselves are elementary.
missed.quote: La donnée d'un F' équivaut à une factorisation analogue pour φ en S →g I' →h I, g surj., h coinit. surj.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor historical interest only: it documents Grothendieck's combinatorial approach to 'figures' and tame topology after the Esquisse. No new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine bookkeeping translation of 'refinement inducing a refinement on a closed subfigure' into factorisation and pullback diagrams of poset-valued maps. Correct and natural, but elementary.
transcription_corrections: Line 'La donnée de G'...': the maps are written g'_J (or g*_J) and h'_J, and φ' = φ|T. The words read roughly 'où g' est une [?] coinit. surjection d'ens. ordonnés, et h' une [?] surjection' (as transcribed, though likely a slip, see errors).
In the NB, the struck word after 'J ⊂ I' appears to be 'fermée' (crossed out), consistent with the transcription.
In the first diagram the left curved arrow is labelled 'f*_J = f|T' and the vertical arrows are g*_J then h_J. The right vertical arrow is labelled 'f surj.'.
Bottom right annotation: 'avec J' = h^{-1}(J)' (a struck symbol precedes J').
